summary: Stream session drift after mobile network path migration (UDP->TCP) causes interleaved partial chunks and missing terminal event
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running SSE streams from their mobile app sometimes arrive with duplicated midstream fragments and the final '\u003cEND\u003e' terminal event never arrives after a path migration (carrier -> wifi) that triggers a UDP-to-TCP transport change. The stream resumes but text fragments are interleaved or truncated, leaving user-visible partial sentences and no closure marker.

Impact:
- Several customers in the account see final outputs missing or partial (2-5% of streams during heavy mobile churn).
- Affects production traffic for Noteable Analytics (self-serve).
- User workflows that depend on terminal metadata (end-of-stream markers / choices) are blocking downstream processing.

Environment:
- prod (us-east), mobile clients on iOS/Android reported.
- Model: redwood/open-rlhf-7b-v2 pinned in customer config.
- Observed across Edge nodes in us-east behind our regional LB.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a streaming SSE request from mobile app on cellular.
2) While stream is open, switch device to wifi or initiate a VPN that forces transport change.
3) Observe resumed stream: some fragments duplicated, other fragments truncated; final terminal event not received.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side request log shows resume/offset exchange completed.
- Client receives resume frames but then receives small interleaved fragments that appear out of order and lacks the final event.
- Trace IDs: trace-us-east-20260312-9a7f3c (attached).

Expected behavior:
- Resume should produce contiguous token stream ending with terminal event (metadata + end marker).

Immediate workaround suggested to customer:
- Reconnect the client and re-run the request (restarts generation).
- For mission-critical workflows, use short-lived non-resumable streams while mobile is expected to change networks.

Attachments / logs:
- Kibana trace: https://kibana.redwood.internal/trace/trace-us-east-20260312-9a7f3c
- Edge proxy logs excerpt: /artifacts/SUP-135318/edge-logs-20260312.txt

Notes: customer supplied a pcap showing a path migration with transition from QUIC/UDP to HTTPS/TCP simultaneous with an auth probe.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Diego Marquez (SRE): Confirmed trace present. Initial hypothesis: resume token mapping may be misapplied when transport changes and edge proxy rewrites session IDs. Gathering edge logs and proxy connection handoff details.

2026-03-14 07:13 - Diego Marquez: Deployed additional logging to edge-proxy canary. Early results: when connection switch co-occurs with auth probe and our LB performs connection draining, we see resumestate IDs reused for a short window leading to interleaved frames. Creating internal task to add stronger session binding (nonce) on resume handshake.
2026-03-14 12:20 - Support: Asked customer to try client-side backoff before resume to see if delaying 300-500ms avoids overlap. Customer testing now.

2026-03-14 15:40 - Elena Novak: Drafted a patch to include per-resume nonce and to reject resume attempts that present mismatched transport metadata. Patch reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/879 (WIP).
investigation_notes: Checked resume handshake logs: server acked resume at offset N, client sent resume token T; edge logs show token T reused after transient LB rebind.

KV cache state shows expected priming for token ranges 0..N but after transport change there are duplicate small fragments in the same stream ID; indicates two partial generators may be merged by edge mapping logic.
Edge proxy connection handoff timeline indicates short window where old socket lingers and new socket replays buffered fragments, producing interleaved message sequence.

Hypothesis: when QUIC->TCP migration occurs, our edge may accept the new connection and map it to the same session ID too quickly, allowing buffered fragments from the previous path to intermix with resumed output. The final terminal event from one connection can be lost if a graceful EOF isn't propagated correctly to the resume controller.
Repro dupe rate increased in tests when auth probe (keepalive) triggers a 100-continue style interim which caused client to reissue resume before server had cleared old socket queue.
resolution: In progress - patch under review and canary deploy in us-east scheduled. Temporary mitigation: recommend client-side delay before resume and server-side reject of resume when transport metadata mismatches.
resolution_notes: Planned change: add per-resume nonce to handshake and require transport-metadata equality (protocol family + local edge instance id) before accepting resume. This prevents cross-transport session reuse.
Short term: edge config updated to hold resume acceptance for 500ms after a socket handoff to allow graceful EOF propagation. Deployed to canary region us-east-1.
Customer-facing: support rep communicated recommended client delay. Customer confirmed they will test backoff and report.
Follow-up: postmortem scheduled if canary validates; update streaming resume runbook and client SDK docs with recommended backoff on network changes.
next_steps: Monitor canary metrics for duplicate-fragment rate and missing terminal events (baseline -> reduce to <0.1%).
If canary is stable for 24h, promote patch to prod in a phased rollout to us-east then global regions.
Coordinate with SDK team to publish client-side recommended backoff release and sample code.
Prepare postmortem and customer notification if impact persists after rollout.
